img: In the night the gale tore the old fence down
text: A single nail lies in the wet grass, still holding a splinter of the post it was driven into. Hagalaz is that nail, what remains when the structure goes down in one night. The field is open now, and the sheep can walk where they were never able to walk before. What will still be standing when you stop holding up the thing you have been holding up?

img: The shavings curl away from the blade
text: The blade stays where the hand holds it, and the shavings fall away in curls. Kenaz is that steady edge, the light that shows you what the wood is doing under your hands. What falls is not waste, it is the shape becoming clear. Kuky, what have you seen in your work that you can no longer unsee?

img: The sweater you knitted all winter is finally finished
text: The sweater lies finished across your lap, sleeves even, the last thread worked in. Jera is the harvest, and here it is the wool that has become something you can wear. You cannot point to the evening it turned from yarn into this. Something in you may be finished already, Kuky, stitched slowly in months you were not counting.

img: You keep knitting though the yarn is almost out
text: The needles keep moving, though the yarn thins toward its last coil in your hand. Nauthiz is that shrinking thread, the plain fact of a need that will not be talked out of itself. You can stitch faster or slower, but the length does not change. Something here is asking to be counted, not carried further.

img: Someone calls your name across the crowd
text: The crowd is loud until one voice carries your name across it, and the noise falls back. Ansuz sits in that moment where sound becomes speech meant for you. What reaches you, Kuky, arrives in someone's particular voice, not in the general din. Whether hearing it plainly draws you closer to that person, or shows you how far apart you stand, is yours to weigh.

img: One hand holds something out, and the other receives it
text: You stand where one hand holds something out and another opens to take it, the space between them narrow and warm. Gebo is that small gap, the place where a gift stops belonging to one person and has not yet settled with the other. Neither hand can close without ending the exchange. Is there something you could hold out without counting, and something offered you could take without hurrying to answer it?

img: In the night the gale tore the old fence down
text: A single nail lies in the wet grass, bent, still holding a splinter of the old post. The gale took the fence in the night, and the field runs on now without a line drawn through it. Hagalaz is the storm that removes what was holding a shape in place. When you choose, will you rebuild the fence where it stood, or walk out into the open ground it was keeping from you?

img: The shavings curl away from the blade
text: The blade stays where the hand holds it, and everything else curls away in pale shavings. Kenaz is that steadiness at the cutting edge, the light by which a maker sees what the wood is becoming. What falls away was never the work, though it had to be cut. Kuky, is there something in your making you now see plainly enough that you cannot go back to not seeing it?

img: The sweater you knitted all winter is finally finished
text: The sweater lies finished across your knees, every row set down on a different evening. Jera is the season come round, what was worked long ago now warm in your hands. You cannot point to the stitch where it became a sweater. Perhaps, Kuky, something in you has been finishing itself this whole time without announcement.

img: You keep knitting though the yarn is almost out
text: The needles keep moving, though the yarn thins toward its end. Nauthiz is the work that continues on what little remains, and the counting that starts anyway. You are close enough to the end of the ball to see it, Kuky, and still the row is unfinished. This may be the point where rest stops being something you earn.

img: Someone calls your name across the crowd
text: The noise of the crowd is still there, and then a voice cuts through it and the rest falls back. Ansuz is that moment, when sound becomes speech meant for you. What reaches you between two people may arrive plainer than the din around it. This is either something being said to you at last, or something you have been hearing and holding at arm's length.

img: One hand holds something out, and the other receives it
text: You stand close enough to see both hands, one holding something out, the other open beneath it. Neither hand moves fast, and the weight passes between them without a word. Gebo is the rune of that passing, the gift and the taking as one act. Is there something you could hold out without counting the return, or something offered you might take with both hands today?

img: You leaf through the guestbook in the mountain hut
text: In the guestbook's margin, a faint crease where someone's thumb rested before they wrote. The page you turn to is empty, and the blank rune sits here as the entry not yet made. Every name above yours went somewhere, Kuky, though the book says nothing of where. Your direction may be one of the things still without a name, and that may be fine for now.

img: You look for the valley's name on the map
text: The map shows ridge, river, road — then a valley where the name should be, and the paper stays empty there. The blank rune is that empty space, the place no one has named yet. You can choose a road by its name, or walk toward the one without. What if the unnamed valley is the choice worth leaving open a while longer, Kuky?

img: The thick fog hides the fjord
text: Where the water ends and the fog begins, there is no line to mark it. The blank rune is that edge, the part of the fjord no one has looked at yet. Something is there, unnamed, neither hidden nor shown. Is there a thing in your life you could leave without a name a while longer?
